members.name: a
members.instructions: This is a chat in which a persuader tries to get the other person (the persuadee) to donate to the charity Save the Children. Classify ONLY the final persuader message (after 'Persuader message to tag') by the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it mainly uses. Earlier lines are context and may be out of order.

criteria.greeting: Opens the chat or exchanges pleasantries: hello, hi, nice to meet you, asking how the other person is doing, or replying to their how-are-you by saying how the persuader is doing (good, well, not bad, pretty good).
criteria.org_identity: Describes what Save the Children is or does: its mission, programs, areas of work, countries served, history, founder, size, partnerships, or current relief efforts.
criteria.org_member: The persuader speaks for the organization: describes their work promoting it and encouraging donations, or reports what we (the organization) do or have raised. If the message asks whether the partner knows the organization, it is a source inquiry.
criteria.role_only: Only states that the persuader works or volunteers for the charity, with nothing about what the charity does and no request.
criteria.org_trust: Vouches for the charity's trustworthiness, reputation, track record or value: lives it has saved, what it has achieved, ratings, share of funds going to programs, accountability, being reputable, well known, or doing important good work, including when said while agreeing with the partner.
criteria.emotion: Tries to stir feelings (sadness, sympathy, guilt) by describing children's suffering: their hardship, violence, hunger, deaths, statistics about children dying or hurt, telling the story of a particular child in need and how they were helped, asking the partner to imagine their situation, or expressing the persuader's own sadness about it.
criteria.logic: Gives a reason or argument why donating is sensible or effective: how donations make a difference, what help achieves for children (a better future, a fair chance), children as the future, everyone should help, comparisons of cost to benefit such as what a given sum per day or month achieves, addressing objections with reasoning.
criteria.small_ask: Lowers the bar by stressing that even a tiny amount counts or is easy to give: any little bit helps, small change, a few cents or a few dollars makes a big difference, start small (the point is how little is needed), including when backed by the persuader's own experience; but if the message mainly expresses sadness or guilt it is an emotional appeal. (A question asking whether they could give a particular small sum is asking for an amount instead. Saying the amount is entirely the partner's choice is donation information instead.)
criteria.process: Explains the mechanics of donating in this task: the allowed amount range, that the partner decides how much and any amount is acceptable, what range of amounts would be typical or appropriate (a range, not a single suggested figure), that it is deducted from the task payment, that the research team collects and forwards donations, when or how to enter the amount, payment methods.
criteria.website: Points the partner to the charity's website or gives a link (URL) for more information.
criteria.ask_amount: Asks how much the partner would like to donate, or asks (as a question) whether they could give a particular amount.
criteria.propose: Asks or urges the partner to donate (would you donate, will you help, please give), including short yes/no questions asking whether they will do it or accept, statements suggesting they donate some of their payment or a particular amount, and short pleas that the children need their help with no reason or suffering described.
criteria.self_donate: The persuader talks about their own personal giving to Save the Children or to this cause: that they donate, have donated, regularly give, will donate now, or will match the partner's donation.
criteria.other_charity: The persuader mentions their own giving to a different, named charity rather than Save the Children.
criteria.story: Tells a narrative about an event in the persuader's own life that makes no persuasive point (rare). A story about a particular child helped by the charity is an emotional appeal instead.
criteria.source_q: Asks whether the partner knows or has heard of Save the Children, or what they know or think about the organization; also the persuader first bringing up Save the Children by name as the charity they want to discuss (a mention of it, without describing its work). Not when answering the partner's question.
criteria.task_q: Asks about the partner's views on or experience with donating money, involvement in charities, helping others, or children's causes in general, including leading or rhetorical questions asking whether they agree that helping or giving is worthwhile, or about their chance to make a difference, and did-you-know questions about charities or giving in general. Not a question asking whether they will donate or accept.
criteria.personal_q: Asks about the partner's own life: family, children, location, job, background, or whether they personally volunteer their time.
criteria.thank: Thanks the partner (for their time, donation, or chatting), possibly with a goodbye.
criteria.praise: Compliments the partner or cheers their decision: says they are kind, generous, a good person, or reacts with a bare one-word-style cheer (great!, awesome!, wonderful!, that's great!) to what they said or decided. Not surprise (wow) and not glad-to-hear or sounds-good reactions.
criteria.ack: Agrees with or reacts to what the partner said, showing it was heard: I agree, that is true, I understand, me too, that makes sense, glad to hear that, great to hear, sounds good, wow, that's interesting. Not when it adds a claim about the charity, and not a bare cheer like great!
criteria.filler: A flat filler with no real content: ok, fine, yeah, sure, alright.
criteria.intro: Only announces the topic, e.g. that the persuader would like to talk about a charity or a cause, without asking for a donation or saying anything about the charity.
criteria.answer: A bare answer to the partner's question (yes, no, I'm not sure, I am familiar with them) that adds no information. An answer that says anything about the charity, its work or its use of funds is not this.
criteria.confirm: Confirms the amount the partner said they will give, or asks them to give more than the amount they stated.
criteria.closing: Says goodbye or wishes a good day without thanking, or says you're welcome.
criteria.offtask: Talks about something unrelated to the charity or donating: weather, the persuader's day or location, the task logistics, insults, chit-chat.
criteria.other: Anything else: fragments, typos, corrections, unclear or meaningless text, URLs alone.
